terms.definition: The IR task setup used throughout: a fixed collection of documents (corpus) is ranked against a query using a relevance score; humans label some query-document pairs as relevant or not (relevance judgments / qrels).
Evaluating a retrieval system on a dataset, domain, or task it was not trained on, as opposed to training and testing on splits of the same dataset.

A classical term-matching ranking formula that scores a document by how often, and how distinctively, it contains the query's words; used here as the untrained lexical baseline. (The letters are not expanded in the source material and are not guessed here.)

Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at rank 10: a rank-aware retrieval metric that rewards relevant documents more when they appear higher among the top 10 results, and works for both yes/no and graded relevance judgments.

terms.term: lexical vs. sparse-neural vs. dense vs. late-interaction vs. re-ranking (architecture families)
terms.definition: The five ways a retriever can be built: lexical = token matching (BM25); sparse-neural = a neural network reweights/expands terms, still matched via an inverted index; dense = query and document each embedded as one vector and matched by similarity ('bi-encoder'); late-interaction = token-level embeddings compared with a lightweight interaction function; re-ranking = a 'cross-encoder' scores each query-document pair jointly, but only for a short candidate list from a first-stage retriever.
An architecture that encodes the query and the document independently into vectors, compared afterward by a similarity function; underlies dense retrieval.

An architecture that encodes the query and a candidate document together, so attention can cross between them; more accurate but must be run separately for every candidate, so it is only used to re-rank a short list.
A late-interaction retriever: computes token-level embeddings for the query and document separately, then aggregates a similarity score with a lightweight (max-similarity) interaction function.
A dense bi-encoder retriever trained with a BM25 hard negative and in-batch negatives, evaluated here as one of the five architecture families.
The share of a system's top-10 retrieved documents that were never judged by the original annotators of a test collection; a high value means the reported score for that system may be understated.

acronym_scope_note: ANCE, SPARTA, TAS-B, GenQ, and 'MS MARCO' are used as proper names of specific systems/datasets and are described functionally at first use (what they do, per project/paper.txt), rather than letter-by-letter expanded, because project/paper.txt itself does not spell out what their letters stand for and inventing an expansion would violate the no-fabrication rule. This is expected to surface as WARN-level 'undefined acronym' lint flags for these five names; reviewed and accepted at the terminology audit (workflow step 14).
